I thought it might be useful to people to forget about hubs in a geodesic altogether. Just get long enough pieces of straight pipe, bend them into dome shape, and then tie them together with other bent pipes using zipties.

There is a video here of how to bend PVC pipe with boiling water.

If you are using sand

  • Calculate how much would be needed to fill the pipe.
  • Get twice that amount of sand.
  • Heat the sand with a blow torch on on a hob in a pan.
  • Stopper one end of the pipe.
  • Use a funnel and protective gloves to pour half the sand into the PVC pipe.
  • Your pipe will now have warmed.
  • Empty the sand.
  • Pour the remaining hot sand into the warm pipe.
  • Bend the pipe to the desired shape. It should be malleable, like a hose.
There is a nice video here of a chap warming the pipe using friction. He then uses a "bending spring" inside the pipe, and bends it to 90 degrees on his knee!

If you are going to bend a lot of long pipe into arcs, this chap has an excellent method, using cheap pipe elbows and a piece of board.

If the nails he used were already in place and very long, you could stack pipes you are bending on top of each other.

If the board is held at the vertical throughout the process, you could additionally use the other side of the board. You would need nails there too, though.

Best Practices for Bending PVC
